name: ADNOC
blurb: ADNOC is Abu Dhabi's state-owned integrated energy group, operating the emirate's onshore and offshore crude fields, the giant Ruwais refining and petrochemical complex, and Das Island LNG facilities.

footprint.note: Operates ~4 million bpd capacity across onshore and offshore Abu Dhabi concessions, one of the world's largest proven reserve bases
Das Island LNG plant has produced liquefied natural gas since 1977, supplying long-term contracts to Asian buyers

assets.name: ADNOC Headquarters
assets.note: Corniche-area headquarters tower overseeing ADNOC Group's upstream, downstream and trading operations

assets.name: Bab Oil Field
assets.note: Major onshore field operated via ADNOC Onshore, producing light crude that feeds the Murban blend

assets.name: Bu Hasa Oil Field
assets.note: Discovered 1962; one of ADNOC Onshore's largest producing fields with capacity around 600,000 bpd

assets.name: Asab Oil Field
assets.note: Onshore field contributing to the Murban crude stream, operated by ADNOC Onshore

assets.name: Sahil Oil Field
assets.note: Onshore concession field in the Bab/Murban producing complex

assets.name: Upper Zakum Oil Field
assets.note: One of the world's largest offshore fields, operated by ADNOC Offshore with Upper Zakum production capacity targeted above 1 million bpd

assets.name: Lower Zakum Oil Field
assets.note: Offshore field operated by ADNOC Offshore, producing Upper Zakum/Umm Shaif-grade crude

assets.name: Umm Shaif Oil Field
assets.note: Legacy offshore field with proven reserves near 3.9 billion barrels, capacity around 300,000 bpd

assets.name: Satah Offshore Field
assets.note: Smaller offshore producing field within the ADNOC Offshore concession

assets.name: Das Island Crude Terminal
assets.note: Historic offshore crude processing, storage and export hub since the 1960s, handling Umm Shaif and Zakum crude

assets.name: Das Island LNG Plant
assets.note: ADNOC LNG's liquefaction plant, operating since 1977, shipping LNG mainly to Japanese and Asian buyers

assets.name: Zirku Island Terminal
assets.note: Offshore island terminal processing and exporting crude from nearby ADNOC Offshore fields

assets.name: Ruwais Refinery Complex
assets.note: One of the world's largest refining complexes with combined capacity over 900,000 bpd, integrated with Borouge petrochemicals

assets.name: Jebel Dhanna Terminal
assets.note: Main onshore crude export terminal near Ruwais serving Murban crude loadings

assets.name: Fujairah Terminal
assets.note: Terminus of the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline, allowing crude exports bypassing the Strait of Hormuz

name: Saudi Aramco
blurb: Saudi Aramco is the world's largest integrated oil and gas company, producing crude at unmatched scale from giant onshore and offshore fields such as Ghawar and Safaniya while expanding downstream refining and building a new international LNG portfolio.

footprint.note: World's top crude producer/exporter, sustainable capacity ~12 mb/d across onshore and offshore giant fields
Building an LNG position via equity stakes in Rio Grande LNG (US) and the MidOcean Energy portfolio rather than domestic liquefaction

assets.name: Aramco Headquarters

assets.name: Ghawar Field

assets.name: Safaniya Field
assets.note: World's largest offshore oil field, ~1.2 mb/d capacity, Arabian Gulf

assets.name: Manifa Field

assets.name: Zuluf Field
assets.note: Major offshore field, ~0.6+ mb/d capacity, Arabian Gulf

assets.name: Marjan Field
assets.note: Offshore field undergoing major expansion, targeting ~1.2 mb/d plus gas/condensate

assets.name: Khurais Field

assets.name: Qatif Field

assets.name: Rio Grande LNG (equity stake)
assets.note: Equity stake and 20-year offtake in NextDecade's Rio Grande LNG export terminal, Brownsville, Texas

name: BHP
blurb: The world's largest miner by market capitalisation, dominated by iron ore and coal but running a growing tracked-commodity copper business plus a nickel unit currently in care and maintenance.

footprint.note: Escondida (world's largest copper mine), Spence and the Copper South Australia hub (Olympic Dam, Carrapateena, Prominent Hill) plus a minority stake in Antamina, Peru.
Nickel West (Mt Keith, Leinster, Kalgoorlie smelter, Kwinana refinery) placed into care and maintenance in late 2024 amid the nickel price downturn, with a review due by 2027.

assets.name: Escondida
assets.note: World's largest copper mine by output; BHP holds 57.5% and operates it, located in the Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region.

assets.name: Spence
assets.note: Wholly-owned open-pit copper mine near Sierra Gorda, Antofagasta Region, expanded via the Spence Growth Option.

assets.name: Olympic Dam
assets.note: Underground copper-uranium-gold-silver mine and integrated smelter/refinery in South Australia; BHP is investing to lift throughput.

assets.name: Carrapateena
assets.note: Underground copper-gold mine in South Australia's Gawler Craton, acquired via the 2023 OZ Minerals takeover; part of Copper South Australia.

assets.name: Prominent Hill
assets.note: Underground/open-pit copper-gold mine in South Australia, also acquired with OZ Minerals in 2023.

assets.name: Oak Dam
assets.note: Deep IOCG copper-gold deposit ~65km south-east of Olympic Dam; under evaluation as a potential fourth South Australian copper mine.

assets.name: Antamina
assets.note: Large copper-zinc mine in Ancash; BHP holds a 33.75% non-operated joint-venture stake alongside Glencore, Teck and Mitsubishi.

assets.name: Mount Keith
assets.note: Large open-pit nickel sulphide mine and concentrator in WA's Northern Goldfields; on care and maintenance since late 2024.

assets.name: Leinster Nickel Operations
assets.note: Underground/open-pit nickel mine and concentrator; part of Nickel West, suspended in the 2024 care-and-maintenance decision.

assets.name: Kalgoorlie Nickel Smelter
assets.note: Nickel matte smelter at Feysville near Kalgoorlie; idled alongside the rest of Nickel West.

assets.name: Kwinana Nickel Refinery
assets.note: Nickel sulphate/briquette refinery south of Perth; on care and maintenance and under strategic review since October 2024.

name: Equinor
blurb: Norwegian state-controlled energy major dominating North Sea oil and gas production, with Europe's largest gas export system and growing Gulf of Mexico and Brazil offshore positions.

footprint.note: Operator of Norway's largest fields (Johan Sverdrup, Troll, Oseberg) plus offshore Brazil and non-operated US Gulf of Mexico interests.
Sole operator of Snøhvit/Melkøya, Norway's only LNG export plant, alongside pipeline gas exports from the Norwegian Continental Shelf.

assets.name: Equinor Headquarters
assets.note: Global headquarters in Forus, Stavanger, overseeing Equinor's Norwegian Continental Shelf and international operations.

assets.name: Johan Sverdrup
assets.note: Giant North Sea field producing roughly a third of Norway's oil output; one of the lowest carbon-intensity oil fields globally, powered from shore.

assets.name: Troll
assets.note: Largest gas field on the Norwegian shelf with a substantial oil rim (Troll Oil), operated by Equinor in the North Sea.

assets.name: Oseberg
assets.note: Long-running North Sea oil and gas field complex with multiple platforms, operated by Equinor since the 1980s.

assets.name: Gullfaks
assets.note: Mature North Sea oil field with three integrated platforms, one of Norway's original giant discoveries operated by Equinor.

assets.name: Snorre
assets.note: Northern North Sea oil field developed via Snorre A and B platforms, undergoing late-life redevelopment for extended production.

assets.name: Johan Castberg
assets.note: Equinor's flagship Barents Sea development on an FPSO, opening a new oil province in Arctic Norway; started production in 2024.

assets.name: Rosebank
assets.note: UK's largest undeveloped oil field, west of Shetland, operated by Equinor with an FPSO development underway.

assets.name: Snøhvit / Melkøya LNG
assets.note: Melkøya liquefaction plant at Hammerfest processes gas piped from the Snøhvit field in the Barents Sea; Norway's only LNG export facility.

assets.name: Mongstad Refinery
assets.note: Norway's largest refinery near Bergen, processing North Sea crude and serving as a major crude oil terminal and logistics hub.

assets.name: Kalundborg Refinery
assets.note: Equinor's Danish refinery on Zealand, supplying fuel products across Scandinavia from North Sea and imported crude.

assets.name: Caesar-Tonga (Gulf of Mexico)
assets.note: Deepwater Green Canyon oil development in the US Gulf of Mexico in which Equinor holds a non-operated working interest.

assets.name: Marcellus Shale (Appalachia)
assets.note: Equinor's onshore shale gas acreage in Pennsylvania, a non-operated feedstock position feeding US domestic and export gas markets.

assets.name: Bacalhau
assets.note: Equinor-operated pre-salt oil development in the Santos Basin using a large-capacity FPSO, one of Brazil's biggest new offshore projects.

assets.name: Peregrino
assets.note: Heavy oil field in the Campos Basin operated by Equinor via two fixed platforms, expanded with the Peregrino Phase 2 project.

assets.note: Volga-region refinery in Samara Oblast, part of the Samara refining hub.

assets.name: Ryazan Refinery (RNPK)
assets.note: One of Russia's largest refineries, near Ryazan south of Moscow, majority-owned by Rosneft.

assets.name: Komsomolsk Refinery
assets.note: Far East refinery at Komsomolsk-on-Amur, Khabarovsk Krai, supplying Pacific and domestic markets.

assets.name: Achinsk Refinery
assets.note: Siberian refinery in Krasnoyarsk Krai serving regional fuel demand.

assets.name: Angarsk Petrochemical Company (ANHK)
assets.note: Integrated refining and petrochemical complex in Irkutsk Oblast, Eastern Siberia.

assets.name: Novorossiysk Export Terminal
assets.note: Key Black Sea crude and product export terminal used by Rosneft for Mediterranean-bound cargoes.

assets.name: De-Kastri Oil Terminal
assets.note: Pacific coast export terminal in Khabarovsk Krai loading crude from the Sakhalin-1 project, in which Rosneft holds a stake.

assets.name: Sakhalin-1 (Chayvo Field)
assets.note: Offshore/onshore field off northeast Sakhalin Island; Rosneft became lead operator after Exxon's 2022 exit.

name: Sonatrach
blurb: Algeria's state oil and gas company and Africa's largest producer, operating the country's giant Saharan crude fields and pioneering LNG export complexes on the Mediterranean coast.

footprint.note: Operates Algeria's major onshore crude fields, pipelines, refineries and export terminals.
World's first LNG exporter (1964); operates Hassi R'Mel gas hub and Arzew/Skikda liquefaction complexes.

assets.name: Hassi Messaoud Oilfield
assets.note: Algeria's largest crude oil field, discovered 1956, anchor of national crude output.

assets.name: Rhourde El Baguel Oilfield
assets.note: Major giant crude field in the Sahara, on stream since the 1960s.

assets.name: Hassi Berkine Sud Oilfield
assets.note: Large crude field developed with international partners, key production growth driver.

assets.name: Ourhoud Oilfield
assets.note: Major crude field in the Berkine Basin, one of Algeria's largest producing assets.

assets.name: Hassi R'Mel Gas Field
assets.note: Algeria's giant gas field and the hub feeding domestic pipelines and LNG export trains.

assets.name: In Salah Gas Complex
assets.note: Major Saharan gas development supplying regional and export pipeline networks.

assets.name: In Amenas Gas Complex
assets.note: Large gas and condensate complex near the Libyan border, feeding export pipelines.

assets.name: Tin Fouye Tabankort (TFT)
assets.note: Gas and condensate field cluster in the Illizi province.

assets.name: Arzew GL1Z/GL2Z LNG Complex
assets.note: Bethioua liquefaction complex including GL1Z, one of the world's first LNG plants (1964).

assets.name: Skikda GL1K LNG Complex
assets.note: Rebuilt Mediterranean coast liquefaction complex, key Europe-facing LNG export hub.

assets.name: Arzew Refinery (RA1Z)
assets.note: Major coastal refining complex processing Saharan crude for domestic and export markets.

assets.name: Skikda Refinery
assets.note: Large Mediterranean refinery paired with the Skikda export and LNG terminal.

assets.name: Algiers Refinery (Sidi Arcine)
assets.note: Refinery serving the Algiers metropolitan fuel market.

assets.name: Arzew Export Terminal (Bethioua)
assets.note: Principal crude and LNG/LPG export terminal on the western Mediterranean coast.

assets.name: Skikda Export Terminal
assets.note: Crude oil and LNG export terminal serving pipeline flows from the Sahara.

assets.name: Bejaia Export Terminal
assets.note: Crude export terminal at the terminus of the Hassi Messaoud-Bejaia pipeline.

assets.name: Sonatrach Headquarters
assets.note: Corporate headquarters in Hydra, Algiers, overseeing upstream, midstream and downstream operations.

name: Vale
blurb: Brazilian mining giant and the world's second-largest nickel producer, with base-metals operations spanning Canada, Brazil and Indonesia alongside its dominant iron ore business.

footprint.note: Vale Base Metals: Sudbury and Voisey's Bay (Canada), Onça Puma (Brazil), PT Vale Indonesia (Sorowako); world #2 nickel producer.
Salobo and Sossego mines in Carajás, Brazil, plus copper concentrate as a by-product of Sudbury nickel ore in Canada.
Recovered as a by-product from Voisey's Bay/Sudbury nickel ore at the Long Harbour hydrometallurgical refinery, Newfoundland.
Azul mine in the Carajás mineral province, Pará, one of the world's largest manganese ore operations.

assets.name: Vale Global Headquarters
assets.note: Corporate HQ on Praia de Botafogo, Rio de Janeiro, overseeing base metals and iron ore businesses worldwide.

assets.name: Sudbury Operations (Copper Cliff Complex)
assets.note: Integrated nickel mining and smelting complex in Ontario; among Vale's oldest and largest nickel operations, active since 1918.

assets.name: Copper Cliff Copper Refinery
assets.note: Refines copper recovered as a by-product of Sudbury nickel-copper ore into cathode.

assets.name: Voisey's Bay Mine
assets.note: Underground nickel-copper-cobalt mine in Labrador; concentrate is shipped to Long Harbour for processing.

assets.name: Long Harbour Nickel Processing Plant
assets.note: Hydrometallurgical refinery in Newfoundland processing Voisey's Bay concentrate into finished nickel, copper and cobalt.

assets.name: Thompson Mine
assets.note: Underground nickel mine in Manitoba; ore is processed at the on-site mill after Vale closed the Thompson smelter/refinery in 2010.

assets.name: Onça Puma Mine & Ferronickel Plant
assets.note: Lateritic nickel mine and ferronickel smelting plant near Ourilândia do Norte, Pará.

assets.name: PT Vale Indonesia - Sorowako
assets.note: Integrated nickel mining and smelting operation on Sulawesi producing ferronickel; Vale holds a majority stake in PT Vale Indonesia.

assets.name: Salobo Mine
assets.note: Large copper-gold mine in the Carajás mineral province, Pará; one of Vale's flagship copper operations.

assets.name: Sossego Mine
assets.note: Copper-gold mine near Canaã dos Carajás, Pará, in operation since 2004.

assets.name: Azul Mine
assets.note: Manganese ore mine within the Carajás mineral complex, Pará, supplying ferroalloy producers worldwide.

assets.name: Goro Plant (former VNC, New Caledonia)
assets.note: Legacy Vale Nouvelle-Calédonie nickel laterite mine and processing plant near Yaté; divested to Prony Resources in 2021.
